messages:
jin: quick heads-up — ran a 'hopscotch' grooming experiment on the staging cluster this morning. tried separating prefill vs decode batch formation and added an intermediate hop-bucket that moves short decodes onto fast-path kernels. noticed weird KV cold hits during the transition window.

maria: can you paste the perf numbers? p95/p99 impact, throughput, tokens/sec?

jin: rough numbers: baseline p95=42ms, experiment p95=50ms (so +8ms), p99 unchanged, overall throughput +3% (tokens/sec), but KV miss rate jumped ~15% during the first 30s of a scale-up event.

sam: 15% KV miss spike seems plausible — we primed fewer prefixes due to smaller prefill batches? what did you use for prefill target?

jin: prefill_target_tokens=48, decode_target_tokens=16, batch_window_ms=8. hop-bucket moves requests with decoded_length<=8 into a dedicated fast-path queue that prefers fused kernels.

leo: curious about kernel affinity selection. did the runtime pick fused_attn or fall back to matmul?

jin: affinity requested: ["fused_attn_v2","matmul_opt"], runtime mostly chose fused_attn_v2 for hop-bucket. but on some GPUs the fused kernel caused longer launch jitter when the KV shard wasn't primed.

maria: can you drop the microtrace snippet and the config you used?

jin: pasted logs and config below. the microtrace shows a KV lookup flurry on prefill -> decode handoff.

```
# config snippet we used
hopscotch:
  prefill_target_tokens: 48
  decode_target_tokens: 16
  batch_window_ms: 8
  kv_warmup_ms: 30
  hop_bucket_threshold: 8
  kernel_affinity: ["fused_attn_v2","matmul_opt"]
```

```
# microtrace (abridged)
[00:00:00.000] prefill enqueue id=aa1 tokens=47 -> batch_id=42
[00:00:00.008] prefill finish id=aa1 kv_lookups=1
[00:00:00.012] decode enqueue id=aa1 hop-bucket move -> fast-path
[00:00:00.013] kernel_launch fused_attn_v2 batch=fast-path latency=2.1ms
[00:00:00.014] kv_miss id=aa1 -> backend fetch (cold)
[00:00:00.045] backend_kv_return id=aa1
```

sam: that backend_kv_return gap (~30ms) is the culprit. if hop-bucket prioritizes fused kernels but KV isn't warmed, we trade p95 for better steady throughput.

leo: thinks we should try an adaptive kv_warmup_ms that ramps with scale events. e.g., if node_alloc event detected, raise kv_warmup_ms by +50ms for the next N requests.

maria: also consider biasing prefill batches to include a tiny prefix of decode tokens for common short-turn scenarios — that should reduce handoff lookups. we tried something like prefill_prefix_carry=4 in earlier experiments.

jin: yep. i can re-run two quick A/Bs: (A) increase kv_warmup_ms to 80ms, keep same batch targets; (B) prefill_prefix_carry=4, kv_warmup_ms=30. will run each for 10m on canary.

maria: good. add metric hooks: kv_miss_rate, hop_bucket_migrations/sec, kernel_switch_count, p95, tokens/sec. also track cost delta.

sam: small nit — instrument kernel selection reasons in traces (why fused vs matmul was chosen). saves debugging time.

leo: agreed. i'll add a quick flag in the kernel-selector to emit "reason" strings for the next canary.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: hopscotch-v2-candidate -> canary (4 nodes) by leo at 11:20 UTC.

jin: thanks. i'll kick off the runs and post results here. acceptance criteria: p95 <= baseline+5ms and kv_miss_rate not > baseline by >5% over steady-state.

maria: if A fails and B passes, we still need to evaluate cost tradeoffs. if neither passes, rollback and iterate on hop-bucket eviction policy.

sam: ping me once runs complete; i'll pull flamegraphs and kernel launch histograms.

jin: will do — running bench command now: `./bench/run_sync.sh --suite=hopscotch --duration=600 --seed=2026`

leo: thanks — good plan. :thumbsup:
